native_delegation.instruction: Use native delegation aggressively for parallelizable work. The parent session remains accountable for Striatum artifacts, write scope, verification, and completion. This is a one-shot supervised invocation: you cannot ask the operator a follow-up question. If a step is ambiguous, choose the most-conservative default that matches the synthesis and proceed; the operator publishes the result on your behalf if your CLI access is denied. For long-running test runs, prefer focused pytest invocations before the wider `make test` to avoid lease expiry beyond ~30 minutes.

Use sub-agents aggressively for bounded independent research, review, and code/test/doc authorship. This is a one-shot supervised invocation: you cannot ask the operator a follow-up question. If permission to call `striatum ack` is denied, write the artifact and exit normally; the operator publishes on your behalf. Do not let native delegation obscure the parent session's artifact and verdict accountability.

Use local sub-agents only for bounded independent work. This is a one-shot supervised invocation: write the artifact in this single call; do not surface strategy and exit without producing the file. When writing finding artifacts, ALL FIVE front-matter fields are required (none are optional): schema_version, artifact_kind, verdict_intent, severity, tags. Use schema_version: "striatum.finding.v1" exactly (not "1"); verdict_intent (not verdict); severity from {low,medium,high,critical} (not none); tags as a JSON array; the `author:` byline is a plain markdown line AFTER the front-matter block, NOT a key inside it. Handoff artifacts (DESIGN.md / HANDOFF.md / BUILD_HANDOFF.md) do not need front matter; just the plain `author:` byline. Do not rely on remote agent-to-agent delegation.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0038 UI features from Codex
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0038: web UI feature additions + Vite/React/TypeScript frontend toolchain. Cover the toolchain bootstrap (package.json, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, Makefile targets, CI node-22-LTS integration, wheel package-data updates for bundled output) and the five feature additions (Edit-affordance promotion, /view/ tree browser, /workflows/new chooser wizard, drag-drop workflow graph editor, syntax-highlighted code viewer). Be specific about island mounting pattern (Jinja2 page shells + React islands; not full SPA).

jobs.title: Design RFC 0038 UI features from Claude Code
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0038 emphasizing first-time-user UX for each new affordance: tree-browser navigation grammar; workflow-chooser wizard step-by-step + preview-before-write; drag-drop graph editor widget set (radio buttons for postures, dropdowns for lane/role enums, file-picker for paths, multi-select for tags); code-viewer syntax-highlighting fallback for unknown filetypes; promoted Edit button visual placement. Address accessibility: focus management on `<dialog>`, ARIA labels, keyboard nav completeness.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0038 UI features from Gemini
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0038 with attention to: cross-platform reality of the Vite build (Linux/macOS, node v22+); npm supply-chain considerations for the dev dependency tree (react, react-flow, shiki, vite, typescript) — list packages, pin strategy, lockfile commit posture, npm audit baseline; build determinism (bundle hash check in CI); wheel package-data semantics for the bundled output; the deployment shape (Jinja2 page shells + React islands, NOT full SPA per RFC 0038's non-goal); browser support matrix (`<dialog>` element + modern ES). Adversarial cases: malicious npm package, build-output drift, frontend bundle bloat, accessibility regressions.

jobs.title: Synthesize RFC 0038 implementation plan
jobs.objective: Reconcile all three fresh design artifacts into one implementation plan. Pick concrete: toolchain (Vite + React + TypeScript per RFC 0038 §1), island layout (per RFC 0038 §2), build integration (per §3), island mounting pattern (per §4), per-feature implementation (5a-5e per §5). State the implementer split clearly: implement_toolchain_codex (Python-side: package.json + vite config + Makefile + CI + Jinja2 Edit-button promotion) and implement_components_claude (TypeScript-side: React island components + tests + docs). Stage the work low-risk-first per RFC 0038 §Implementation Plan.

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX review of RFC 0038 design
jobs.objective: Review the synthesized RFC 0038 plan under ergonomics_dx posture. Verdict acceptance means the affordances are discoverable and consistent from a first-time-user perspective. Evaluate: tree browser navigation grammar; chooser wizard step-by-step + preview-before-write; drag-drop graph editor widget choices; code viewer syntax highlighting; promoted Edit button visual placement; accessibility (keyboard nav, focus management, ARIA labels); toolchain choice honest (Vite + React + TS, no scope creep into full SPA); island deployment shape preserved. IMPORTANT: write the REVIEW.md artifact directly with valid striatum.finding.v1 front matter (schema_version: "striatum.finding.v1" exact; ALL FIVE fields).

jobs.title: Implement RFC 0038 V1 toolchain + Jinja2 + CI (codex)
jobs.objective: Implement the Python-side toolchain half of accepted RFC 0038 V1: `src/striatum/web/frontend/{package.json,vite.config.ts,tsconfig.json}`, Makefile targets (`ui-install`, `ui-build`, `ui-dev`, `ui-test`), CI node-22-LTS step + bundle hash check, pyproject.toml package-data for `src/striatum/web/static/build/`, Jinja2 template updates (promote Edit affordance to primary button next to 'Run this workflow now', add island mount points to base.html / view templates / workflow_detail.html / workflow_edit.html / workflows_index.html), service.py route additions if needed (e.g., `GET /v1/repo/tree`). Do NOT write into the frontend src tree (`src/striatum/web/frontend/src/`) — that's claude's scope. Use sub-agents aggressively. This is a one-shot invocation; do not ask follow-ups.

jobs.title: Implement RFC 0038 V1 React islands + docs (claude_code)
jobs.objective: Implement the TypeScript-side component half of accepted RFC 0038 V1: React island components under `src/striatum/web/frontend/src/islands/{tree-browser,workflow-chooser,workflow-graph-editor,code-viewer}/` using react-flow + shiki where the synthesis names them; shared utilities under `src/striatum/web/frontend/src/shared/`; entry points in `src/striatum/web/frontend/src/main.ts`; JS unit tests under `src/striatum/web/frontend/src/__tests__/`. Documentation: new `docs/FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT.md`, HOW_TO_HUMAN updates linking to new web routes, UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE entries for the new component concepts, CHANGELOG entry, RFC 0038 status block update, RFC 0038 index entry update. Do NOT write into the toolchain scope (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, etc.) — that's codex's. Use sub-agents aggressively. This is a one-shot invocation; if striatum ack is denied, write artifacts and exit normally.

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX build review from Codex
jobs.objective: Review the RFC 0038 V1 implementation under ergonomics_dx posture. Focus on the toolchain side: Vite config correctness, bundle hash check in CI, wheel package-data path semantics, Makefile target ergonomics (clear errors when node is missing, sensible defaults), Jinja2 template changes (Edit-button promotion visually right, island mount points correct).

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX build review from Claude
jobs.objective: Review the RFC 0038 V1 implementation under ergonomics_dx posture. Focus on the components side: React island affordance discoverability (tree browser navigation grammar; chooser wizard step ordering + preview-before-write; graph editor widget choices; code viewer language detection); accessibility (keyboard nav, focus management on dialogs, ARIA labels); documentation quality (FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT.md complete + accurate; HOW_TO_HUMAN walkthroughs specific).

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX build review from Gemini
jobs.objective: Review the RFC 0038 V1 implementation under ergonomics_dx posture from the adversarial angle the other two reviewers may miss. Focus on: npm supply-chain hygiene (lockfile committed, package set narrow, no unused deps); build determinism (CI bundle hash check working); cross-platform reality (Vite builds on Linux + macOS identically); browser support matrix (modern only, no polyfills); bundle bloat; accessibility regressions; failure modes (npm install offline, node missing, malformed package.json).
